\section{Authoritative definitions and claim boundaries}
\label{sec:definitions}

\subsection{Operation and endpoint}

\Term{SCI-CAL v0.1 operation.} On admitted \code{xs} support, SCI-CAL binds
each target acquisition occurrence to one row occurrence in one exact selected
immutable observation-specific child APT, applies that row's absolute
\code{flxscale} once without reinterpreting its producer-owned meaning,
applies one supported target-observation atmosphere correction to the
top-of-atmosphere plane, and propagates conditional measurement uncertainty.
It ends at calibrated detector samples, not at a map, fitted source, or
integrated photometric estimate.

\Term{Point-source-peak \(\mjybeam\).} The label denotes a peak-normalized
response convention. For an unresolved source of top-of-atmosphere flux
density $S$ mJy, a downstream map whose realized beam, mapmaker, kernel, and
filter response has unit peak for the declared response basis has ideal peak
$S\ \mjybeam$. This definition does not authorize surface-brightness,
per-pixel, temperature, extended-source, or integrated-flux interpretation.

\Term{Reference plane.} The target is top of atmosphere with
$X_{\rm ref}=0$. A target sample at airmass $X_{ot}$ is corrected from its
observing plane to that reference. Atmosphere corrections used while deriving
the selected source APT belong to that APT's ancestry; they do not replace or
duplicate the target-observation correction.

\subsection{Identity and immutable selection}

\Term{Acquisition occurrence.} The tuple of observation/Tune context,
network or interface, and network-local channel/tone slot. It identifies the
target measured occurrence to which a sample column is bound.

\Term{Measured-APT row occurrence.} The tuple of immutable selected-artifact
identity, its artifact-local row key, and source observation/network context.
A UID is local to that immutable artifact. It is not a universal detector
name.

\Term{Source APT and observation-specific child APT.} The source APT is the
producer-owned Beammap calibration artifact whose row supplies the scientific
meaning and generating lineage of \code{flxscale}. The selected child APT is
the exact immutable observation-specific artifact chosen or produced by
TolProj from an admitted target-to-source association and, if applicable, one
explicitly approved transformation. An identity transformation is recorded
when the source row is selected unchanged. Parent and child occurrences remain
distinct even when their values are numerically equal.

\Term{Association edge.} A separate, directed target-to-source relation that
names both occurrence-scoped endpoints, matcher method and version,
disposition, and available quality evidence. Only a unique admitted match is
sufficient for calibration. Aggregate matcher performance is not a per-row
match probability.

\Term{Identity layers.} Acquisition identity, measured-APT identity,
cross-observation association, and optional design identity answer different
questions. Occurrence identity, order-independent semantic-content identity,
and exact byte-transport identity are also distinct. Equal row numbers, local
keys, paths, timestamps, or integer spellings do not prove correspondence.

\Term{Binding.} Either an explicit keyed relation or a verified ordered-row
contract may bind acquisition occurrences to sample columns and selected APT
rows. An ordered relation is valid only with recorded scope, cardinality,
ordering definition, and proof. Row position alone is not identity.

\Term{Producer--transformer--delivery--consumer boundary.} Beammap/source-APT
production owns the source calibration, source atmosphere, estimator,
beam/template normalization, pointing treatment, spectral convention,
uncertainty, and published factor meaning. TolProj owns target-to-source
association and only an explicitly approved child transformation with its
lineage. TolTECA may deliver the selected immutable artifact into Citlali but
does not change its scientific meaning or value. SCI-CAL consumes the exact
selected child value, applies it once with target atmosphere, and does not
rederive or reinterpret producer or transformer quantities.

\subsection{Factors and once-only lineage}

\Term{Factor instance.} A value together with a stable instance identity,
scientific role, direction, unit, recipient identity, support, reference
plane, validity, application stage, uncertainty status, and parent lineage.
Numerically equal values with different roles are not interchangeable.

\Term{Selected absolute factor.} $F^{\rm sel}_{od}$ is the selected child-APT
row's \code{flxscale}, oriented under the contract as
\(\mjybeam/U_{x,d}\). It is the sole absolute detector factor in the v0.1
signal multiplier. Its scientific meaning resolves to the source-calibration
producer record. If TolProj created a transformed child APT, every approved
transformation, including an embodied pointing-derived correction, is an
ancestry event already represented in this value. Open decisions Q01, Q03,
Q04, and Q05 limit the physical unit, derivation, transfer, and broadband
claims exactly as recorded in Section~\ref{sec:eng-owner-gates}; the contract
orientation alone does not close them.

\Term{Relative responsivity.} \code{responsivity} may support a separately
declared relative-response, diagnostic, normalization, or nuisance role. It
does not independently establish an absolute \(\mjybeam\) scale and is not an
additional v0.1 signal multiplier.

\Term{Sensitivity.} Beammap \code{sens} is a separately typed sensitivity or
approximate-weight quantity. It is neither atmospheric extinction nor an
absolute signal factor nor a general total uncertainty.

\Term{Opaque total factor.} An unqualified \code{fcf} is not authoritative.
A compatibility value can be admitted only when its exact contents, units,
direction, exclusions, and constituent instance identities reproduce the
canonical factorization without omission or duplication.

\Term{Once-only composition.} Each required physical role contributes once
to a realized multiplier. Causal derivation order is recorded in lineage;
numeric multiplication of admitted scalar factors is order independent. A
factor already materialized into a selected artifact is not multiplied again
at execution.

\subsection{Atmosphere operator and passband status}

\Term{Structural operator.} The retained operator identity
\code{am12_fixed_djf25_piecewise_linear_los_tau_v1} is adopted only as a
piecewise-linear function of line-of-sight optical depth with an analytic zero
anchor, exact declared nodes, continuity, and positive finite transmission and
correction. Its content-bound node record, ordinate orientation, and numeric
support are not present in the author packet and therefore remain unresolved
for operational evaluation in this draft.

\Term{Passband reference.} The only selected passband identity is
\begin{center}
\small\code{toltec-passband-set-v1:sha256:}\\
\code{5e6f38f14bcae93a29ffe8362c52b15209f51aee4e48373b23aaa5ec2f8a6433}.
\end{center}
It binds one array-named modeled curve for each TolTEC array and an index. The
frequency coordinate is in GHz and the supplied throughput is dimensionless.
The curves are neither peak-normalized nor area-normalized. Detector or
network aggregation, telescope measurement, uncertainty and covariance,
normalization semantics, original generation recipe, and photon-versus-energy
physical convention are not established. The passband identity can identify
an input to a declared operator; it cannot, by itself, establish that
operator's physical truth.

\Term{Photometric-convention state.} The record connecting source-APT
\code{flxscale}, target-atmosphere evaluation, and reported \(\mjybeam\)
meaning names the per-array reference frequency or wavelength, reference
spectrum, calibrator/color treatment, passband weighting and variation, and
compatibility disposition. Until Q05 is resolved, complete monochromatic mJy
meaning and cross-array spectral interpretation are unavailable rather than
inferred from the unit token.

\Term{Pipeline boundary/order state.} The exact pre-CAL signal and affine
boundary, together with its declared relation to detector mixing,
common-mode/PCA operations, temporal filtering, weighting, mapmaking, and
downstream response. Until Q02 is resolved, local CAL algebra remains
separate from a unique end-to-end transfer-function claim.

\subsection{Uncertainty and response}

\Term{Conditional measurement uncertainty.} Variance, inverse variance, or
covariance of the admitted measurement conditional on fixed factor,
atmosphere, identity, selection, and response state. Its propagation is exact
for the fixed affine operator.

\Term{Nuisance uncertainty.} Uncertainty in calibration, atmosphere, or
response state, with named correlation scope. It is not included in a
conditional weight unless explicitly incorporated through a documented joint
covariance. Missing nuisance uncertainty is unavailable, not zero.

\Term{Response basis.} The originating Beammap APT beam/template occurrence,
including elliptical parameters and their units/frame when available,
together with the separately supplied realized mapmaker, kernel, and filter
response required to interpret a downstream point-source peak. A
circularization is a labeled approximation, never silent replacement.

\subsection{Validity and quality tuple}

An immutable owner-decision snapshot accompanies the tuple below. It records
Q01--Q09 state, owning authority, evidence required, resolution source/date,
and blocked claim or output. It conditions the affected tuple field or claim
without adding an unrelated failure to every other quantity.

Every coherent observation or explicitly declared segment has a state tuple
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal V=(R,E,S,Q,U_c,U_n,B),
 \label{eq:validity-tuple}
\end{equation}
where $R$ is requested mode, $E$ effective mode, $S$ calibrated-signal
validity, $Q$ one segment-level opacity quality class, $U_c$ conditional
uncertainty availability, $U_n$ nuisance/total-uncertainty completeness, and
$B$ response-basis completeness. Required reason codes accompany every
non-success state. In particular:

\begin{itemize}
\item \Term{science-qualification-eligible} means structurally admissible
  under the v0.1 policy with fully resolved scientific inputs. It is an
  eligibility state, not an achieved \code{science-qualified} or
  \code{calibrated-science} claim. Unless the owner later defines a different
  explicit threshold, either achieved claim additionally requires separately
  accepted atmosphere-representation-fidelity and observational-performance
  evidence over the same declared identity and support;
\item \Term{engineering-only unavailable} means the opacity is in
  $0.15<\tau_{225}\leq0.25$, for which no calibrated SCI-CAL output is
  authorized in v0.1;
\item \Term{outside-supported calibration} means the request lies outside an
  admitted domain or lacks a required operator/input identity;
\item \Term{disabled/uncalibrated} records an intentional effective no-op and
  never relabels uncalibrated numbers; and
\item \Term{uncertainty unavailable} may coexist with a valid calibrated
  signal when the missing item is not required to define the signal, but it
  prohibits the corresponding uncertainty or significance claim.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Three claim layers}
\label{sec:claim-layers}

\begin{longtable}{L{0.22\linewidth}L{0.34\linewidth}L{0.36\linewidth}}
\caption{Claims that must not be conflated.}\label{tab:claim-layers}\\
\toprule
Claim & What it establishes & What it does not establish \\
\midrule
\endfirsthead
\toprule
Claim & What it establishes & What it does not establish \\
\midrule
\endhead
Structural calibration correctness & applicable owner gates, typed inputs, producer/transformer/delivery/consumer lineage, valid association, exact factor algebra, once-only lineage, supported operator evaluation, uncertainty transform, and reconstructible output & truth of the atmosphere model, universal transfer, complete broadband meaning, telescope response, repeatability, absolute flux accuracy, or production readiness \\
Atmosphere representation fidelity & agreement of the declared finite operator with a named higher-fidelity atmosphere calculation over declared support & agreement with the actual atmosphere, WVR accuracy, telescope passband truth, or source recovery \\
Observational calibration performance & repeatability and absolute recovery against independent astronomical evidence with full covariance & structural correctness by itself or universal performance outside the studied population and support \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

The prior goals of at most about one-percent atmosphere representation error,
about five-percent relative repeatability, and about five-to-ten-percent
absolute accuracy per band are validation targets only. They are not
guarantees and are not used to fill missing evidence.
